title: AI search citations — why your chatbot cites the 'unlocked web'
summary: High-credibility sites (Consumer Reports, ~60% of top news) block GPTBot, Google's AI crawler and Common Crawl, so AI search reads only what's left: AI-written pages and self-ranking listicles. One in six cited sources is AI-written and models often do post-hoc citation, writing the answer first and finding sources after.
takeaways: Click every AI citation and check the answer is actually on that page
Quality publishers disallow AI crawlers in robots.txt, so AI search skews to low-quality sources
Treat listicles cited by AI as possibly brand self-ranking

title: PPF Contact Solver — ZOZO's open-source GPU cloth and soft-body physics
summary: ZOZO open-sourced ppf-contact-solver, its internal virtual try-on physics engine: penetration-free fabric, rope and soft-body simulation with strain limits, up to 180M contacts, full GPU acceleration, a Blender plugin and a JupyterLab interface.
takeaways: Drop-in production-grade cloth sim for Blender without clipping artifacts
GPU solver scales to massive contact counts for VFX and digital fashion

title: Qwen 3.8 27B — local agentic model that fits on one 24GB GPU
summary: Alibaba's Qwen 3.8 27B quantizes to ~17GB at 4-bit, running on a single RTX 3090/4090, and Qwen's own benchmarks claim 84.3 on OSWorld plus wins on SWE-Bench Pro. Gated DeltaNet layers keep a compact running memory instead of full attention, and it preserves reasoning across tool-call steps, so pair it with an agent harness rather than chatting.
takeaways: A 4-bit 27B model leaves room for real context on a 24GB card
Benchmarks are vendor-reported, wait for independent evals
Use it as the brain of a local agent with scoped file/terminal/browser access

title: Scroll-scrubbed product animation — Apple-style image sequence with AI
summary: Four-step recipe: generate start and end frames in Google Flow, animate between them with frames-to-video, export 30fps frames with Easy GIF, then have your AI coding tool build a scroll-linked canvas image sequence. Same trick Apple uses on product pages.
takeaways: Two keyframes plus AI interpolation gives a product spin/build clip
Export to a 30fps frame sequence and scrub it on a canvas with scroll position

title: OSINT recon trio — open databases, 135-check footprint, GitHub leak alerts
summary: Three unnamed open-source OSINT tools: one finds exposed databases from a single domain, one runs 135 recon and security checks to map a company's attack surface, and one monitors GitHub commits for leaked API keys and passwords with Telegram alerts. Tool names are gated behind a comment-for-link.
takeaways: Monitor public GitHub commits for leaked secrets in your own org
Tool names are not given, so you need to find equivalents yourself

title: ASCILINE — 30fps video streamed as colored text over WebSockets
summary: ASCILINE converts real video server-side into binary-packed text sent over WebSockets, and the browser repaints colored block characters on a canvas at 360p/30fps. No video element, so it slips past video blockers and works on weak connections; frames can also be piped to local LLMs.
takeaways: Video can be delivered as text frames with no media element
Useful pattern for low-bandwidth or terminal-style visuals

title: Claude setup purge — audit stale CLAUDE.md rules for newer models
summary: Argues rules and skills written for older Claude models now hold newer ones back, citing Anthropic cutting much of its system prompt after Opus 5. Recommends a prompt that audits every CLAUDE.md rule and skill, deletes dead weight and rebuilds a lean setup; the prompt itself is comment-gated.
takeaways: Periodically audit CLAUDE.md and skills for rules newer models no longer need
Over-instruction can make capable models perform worse

title: Vibe-coded app performance — five fixes Claude usually skips
summary: Five backend/frontend performance gaps in AI-written apps: uncompressed JSON responses, row-by-row database inserts, a single dependency bottleneck in round-trip latency, no optimistic UI updates, and server re-rendering HTML for every visitor instead of caching.
takeaways: Enable gzip/brotli on API responses
Batch database writes
Profile round-trip latency to find the one step taking ~90% of time
Update UI optimistically and cache rendered pages

title: Agent workspace file tree — persistent memory and context folder layout
summary: A folder structure for Claude-based agents: a brain folder with CLAUDE.md and model routing, five business context files, a memory folder with session logs and an index, per-project context files, NOW.md short-term memory, skills/workflows/scripts folders, Obsidian + GitHub versioning, Notion tasks, and secrets in a gitignored .env.
takeaways: Give agents a stable file tree so memory survives across sessions
Keep a per-project context file plus a short-term NOW file
Put secrets in .env and gitignore it before the first push

title: Self-study pipeline — saved links to AI-generated study guides and quizzes
summary: Save videos and articles via Chrome extensions or text into a table, then give your agent a skill that groups recent saves by topic and generates study guides and quizzes, optionally through NotebookLM. Active recall instead of passive watching.
takeaways: Log what you save in one table so an agent can batch it
Turn saved content into quizzes for active recall

title: Claude Code Meta ads — agent-run campaigns via Meta API repo
summary: A paid-social veteran recommends a ~1,100-star GitHub repo of skills that lets Claude Code run Meta ad campaigns through the Meta API: it walks you through API key setup, generates creatives and copy, and manages Ads Manager. Repo name is comment-gated; anecdotal ROAS claims.
takeaways: Claude Code can operate Meta ads end-to-end via API
Giving an agent card-linked ad spend needs hard budget caps

title: Grok Bot — persistent AI workers sharing one cloud computer
summary: xAI's Grok Bot gives each user one dedicated cloud computer shared by all their bots, which can spawn long-lived bots, hand off work and switch underlying models. Docs warn bots share files, browser sessions and credentials, so they are not a security boundary.
takeaways: Shared-computer agents trade isolation for easy handoffs
Don't rely on separate bots to isolate credentials

title: Vibe-coded app legal risks — ten compliance gaps that get you sued
summary: Ten liability traps for indie apps with rough per-user fines: missing or incomplete privacy policy (data collection, AI use, third parties), undeleted uploads, public storage buckets, fake testimonials, hard-to-cancel subscriptions, silent trial auto-charges, and chatbots without self-harm handling.
takeaways: Privacy policy must disclose data collection, AI use and third-party processors
Make canceling as easy as signing up and send trial-end reminders
Lock storage buckets and actually delete uploads you promise to delete

title: MacBook notch agent monitor — software answer to OpenAI's agent controller
summary: Instead of OpenAI's $230 hardware controller for babysitting coding agents, the creator had Claude build a MacBook notch app showing which agents are working, need attention or are done, with jump-to-session and permission approvals. Build guide is comment-gated.
takeaways: Multi-agent supervision is a UI problem, a status surface solves it
A notch or menu-bar indicator can replace terminal babysitting

title: AI weekly roundup — Pocket TTS, Hermes Skills Hub, Kimi K3 in pure C
summary: Six releases: Kyutai Pocket TTS (100M-param local voice cloning, 6x real-time), Nous Research Hermes Skills Hub (90k agent skills), Grok Imagine Image 2.0 regional editing, Meta Muse Code terminal agent with parallel worktrees, Qwen3.8-Max (2.4T MoE, 1M context), and kimi-k3-in-c, a 176KB C99 engine streaming experts from disk to run a 2T model with no GPU.
takeaways: kimi-k3-in-c streams MoE experts from disk so huge models run CPU-only
Pocket TTS gives free local voice cloning with one-command setup

title: Evo-designed bacteriophages — AI genomes that beat human gene swaps
summary: Science paper: researchers fine-tuned Evo 1 and Evo 2 on 14,466 phage sequences to generate PhiX174-like genomes, and 16 were viable. One (Evo 536) used a G4 packaging protein swap humans had failed to engineer, and recombined AI phages overcame E. coli resistance within 1-5 rounds. Visuals are illustrative, made with Seedance 2.5.
takeaways: Genome language models can satisfy overlapping-gene constraints humans struggle with
Recombination between AI designs produced the resistance breakers

title: Faceless horror channel pipeline — AI agent sourcing, human voice and edit
summary: Argues against fully AI faceless-channel courses: have an agent scrape a horror subreddit (with credit), generate clips with a video model, then hire a human narrator and editor (or use Descript). AI handles admin and sourcing, humans keep the creative part.
takeaways: Use agents for sourcing and hiring, not the creative voice
AI voiceover hurts retention, real narrators win

title: Claude website design stack — Kowalski, Impeccable and taste skills plus MCP
summary: Install the Emil Kowalski design and Impeccable skills for layout, type and motion, add a taste skill that pulls inspiration from real sites, then connect Figma MCP and Playwright so Claude can design, build and visually test websites.
takeaways: Design skills give Claude better defaults for spacing, type and animation
Playwright closes the loop so the agent checks its own render

title: Bilevel autoresearch loops — an outer coach loop rewrites the search
summary: Builds on Karpathy's autoresearch loop (try change, test, keep or revert). An outer coach loop watches the inner worker and rewrites its search playbook so it stops repeating the same ideas; claimed ~5x better on Karpathy's benchmark with the same models.
takeaways: Single loops collapse onto a few favorite ideas
Add an outer loop that edits the inner loop's strategy, not the code

title: MiniMax H3 — unified multi-reference video model with open weights coming
summary: MiniMax H3 generates 4-15s video at up to 2K with stereo sound, combining motion from a video, character from an image and voice from audio in one job. Uses contextual omni-representation training and the H3VAE tokenizer, regenerates low-res output at 2K from the original references, is on the MiniMax API, and weights are promised.
takeaways: One model handles motion transfer, character ref and sound together
Open weights would make it locally adaptable

title: Conway's Law — your product ships your org chart
summary: Melvin Conway's 1967 observation: systems copy the communication structure of the organization that builds them. Modern teams apply the reverse Conway maneuver, designing the target architecture first and then shaping teams to match.
takeaways: Awkward product seams usually map to teams that barely talk
Arrange teams to match the architecture you want

title: Shell sort — gap-based insertion sort that moves items far early
summary: Shell sort runs insertion sort on elements separated by a shrinking gap, letting small values travel long distances early. By the final gap-1 pass the list is nearly sorted, so insertion sort finishes quickly.
takeaways: Gapped passes fix insertion sort's one-step-at-a-time weakness
Final pass with gap 1 is cheap on nearly sorted data

title: AI weekly roundup — Codex Micro controller, LingBot-Map, robot MMA
summary: Carousel of the week's AI news: OpenAI's $230 Codex Micro agent controller, China's robot MMA fight, Netflix using gen AI in ~300 productions, GPT-5.6 driving Blender via Blender MCP, open-source LingBot-Map building real-time 3D maps from video without LiDAR, free Claude for K-12 teachers, and Claude Fable 5 going permanent.
takeaways: LingBot-Map gives LiDAR-free 3D mapping from plain video at ~20 FPS
Blender MCP lets an LLM build full 3D scenes
